name: Five-finger tendon hand
description: Five tendon-driven fingers and a servo-driven wrist rotation. Each finger's SG90 lies in the forearm with a printed two-groove spool: the flexor runs on the palm side through all three joints, the extensor over their backs.

links.label: forearm shell: five SG90 pockets, sheath stops, wrist servo inside
wrist disc on the wrist servo's horn

hardware.note: one flexor and one extensor run per finger, spool groove to fingertip eyelet
3 mm OD; cut one sheath per tendon from its forearm stop to the palm
one per hinge, lengths as drawn; 2.4 mm clearance holes

notes: Each finger's middle and tip joints follow its knuckle by fixed ratios (1.0 and 0.75), standing in for how one flexor shares its pull between three joints; the spool radii are fitted so the line the spool takes up matches what the joints take up, and the lab shows what slack or stretch remains.
Not simulated: line stretch, friction in the sheaths and eyelets, grip force.
Six SG90s draw far more than the Uno's USB fuse allows when they move together; the template powers them from a 5 V bench supply with a ground shared with the Uno.
Assembly: print the parts, pin each hinge with an M2 screw and nut, thread each line from its spool groove through its sheath and the palm channel to the eyelets, tie it at the fingertip.
